newsitem.title: CANADA: Bema, Arizona upbeat on Cerro Casale.
newsitem.headline: Bema, Arizona upbeat on Cerro Casale.

text.p: Bema Gold Corp and Arizona Star Resource Corp said Thursday they were pleased with the latest drill results from their Cerro Casale project and estimated it contains at least 500 million tonnes of economically mineable mineralized material.

The companies said earlier that 14 holes at the property in Chile had an average grade of 1.24 grams per tonne gold and 0.40 percent copper. Excluding two higher grade breccia holes, the average grade is 0.92 grams per tonne gold and 0.35 percent copper. Bema has 49 percent of the project and Arizona Star has 51 percent. Bema controls 30 percent of Arizona Star.
"We're saying there is a billion tonnes of mineralized material and half a billion of that is economically viable," Bema president Clive Johnson told a conference call.
"We're comfortable it is in excess of 500 million tonnes and could get much larger than that," he said.
Executives of the two companies reiterated that they feel the deposit will ultimately be proven to contain at least 15 million ounces of gold and said that could be expanded.
"Half the ore body is still open and open at depth. It has good potential to keep growing," said Johnson.
More drill results are expected in December.
The latest results are in line with previously announced findings and help confirm the dimensions, grade and continuity of the main sulphide porphyry zone.
The companies said they were especially pleased with a high gold content relative to the copper content in the deposit.

They declined to second guess how their stocks would react to the news. Drill results released in August caused Bema's stock to soar but it has recently weakened, a move Johnson attributed to general investor nervousness over exploration stocks.

Asked whether Bema would be interested in selling its stake in Arizona to help finance the project, Johnson said he was "more interested in increasing than decreasing" the position but remained open to whatever would be in the best of shareholders.

Banks have already expressed interest in financing the project, he said. A large-scale mine would likely take four the five years to develop, cost $1 billion and entail a 100,000-plus tonne per day processing plant, the companies said.
